**STEP 1 - Scene:** Two fresh rice-paper summer rolls on a white ridged plate, photographed from above on a dark cloth. Only the plate's food counts.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The plate is about 20 cm in diameter (side-plate size). Area = 3.14 × (10)² ≈ 314 cm². Each roll is about 11 cm long and 3 cm across.

**STEP 3 - Items:** Lettuce, rice-paper wrapper, shredded carrot, pink shrimp or pork pieces, and some herbs or vermicelli.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The two rolls cover about 66 cm², roughly 21% of the plate. Lettuce and wrapper are the main visible areas.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Each roll is roughly a 3 cm diameter cylinder, about 77 ml, so about 155 ml for both. Splitting that by item gives about 45% lettuce, 20% wrapper, 15% carrot, 15% protein, and 5% herbs.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Using bulk densities, lettuce ≈ 70 ml × 0.15 ≈ 10–12 g. Wrapper is thin and hydrated, so I estimate about 20 g. Carrot ≈ 14 g. Shrimp ≈ 18 g. Herbs and vermicelli ≈ 4 g. Total ≈ 68 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Lettuce ≈ 2 kcal, wrapper ≈ 50 kcal (≈250 kcal/100 g), carrot ≈ 6 kcal, shrimp ≈ 15 kcal (≈85 kcal/100 g), herbs ≈ 2 kcal. Total ≈ 75 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Two fresh summer rolls of this size typically weigh about 60–80 g and provide about 70–100 kcal, so the estimate is plausible. The main uncertainty is the wrapper and the protein content.
